messages:
kevin: Heads-up — I sketched a proposal for a lightweight `X-Token-Provenance` header to help quota routing + billing attribution when SAs impersonate across orgs/projects. Want feedback before I dump this into the RFC doc.

maria: Nice, can you paste an example? Curious how granular it is (org vs project vs SA). :eyes:

kevin: Sure — idea is minimal key/value pairs, single header, parseable on edge for routing decisions and later for console display. Example:

```
X-Token-Provenance: org=org-42;project=proj-17;actor=sa:billing-agent;via=impersonation
```

kevin: We use `actor` for the effective caller, `via` for the auth flow (impersonation|direct|exchange), and optional `origin_region` later if needed.

anya: Two quick concerns: 1) authenticity — how do we trust this header? 2) privacy — does it leak org IDs to services?

kevin: Good calls. Plan is edge-injected only after token validation. The header will be added by the auth proxy (not client-supplied). We won't allow clients to set it.

sam: For privacy, we can redact org/project in low-trust downstream or only surface full provenance in console/audit logs if requester has access. In metrics we can hash the ids to preserve aggregation without exposing raw ids.

nico: Also think about caching/batching: many inference requests reuse KV cache and may lose per-request provenance if cached response returned. Need to ensure per-request provenance flows through cache keys or we risk misattributing tokens.

kevin: Agree — we plan to include provenance in cache-key computation for any cached artifacts used for billing/latency attribution. That will avoid mixing attributions, though it slightly increases cache cardinality.

maria: Telemetry side: suggest new metrics names: `token.provenance.impressions`, `token.provenance.cost_tokens`, `token.provenance.latency_p50/p95`. Sampling: keep full attribution for errors and a 5% sample for normals.

anya: UX question for Console: how do we show "effective project" when a request crosses org boundaries? Users get confused when billing shows one project but logs show another.

kevin: Proposal: Console should show two columns in traces and cost view — "Declared Project" (the project bound to key) and "Effective Project" (the provenance actor). Hover text explains impersonation/consent. Default view groups by Effective Project for billing, but allow toggle.

console-bot: note — adding a new column may impact pagination and export. Recommend CSV schema v2 if we add fields.

sam: Rollout plan idea: canary to 10% of traffic behind a feature flag, enable provenance in telemetry only (no UI changes), compare attribution deltas for a week, then enable console surfaces.

maria: Also add a migration doc for partners who use raw logs. We'll provide a script to map old attributions to new header fields.

nico: One more: rate limiting/quotas. If we route by Effective Project for quota, we need to decide precedence when declared project has higher quota than effective project. Fallback rules?

kevin: Default: enforce strictest (lowest) quota between declared and effective to avoid abuse. We can build an override policy later for enterprise configs. Documenting now so it's not ambiguous.

anya: Sounds reasonable. I'll open a short RFC PR with the header spec + parsing rules + telemetry names. Can you add the cache-key change as a separate ops note?

kevin: Will do. PR incoming in ~1h. Thanks for quick notes. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: scheduled rollout job created: featureflag/token_provenance canary -> 10% at 2026-04-02T18:00Z

maria: Great — can we add an alert if attribution delta > 5% during canary? Might catch config mistakes early.

kevin: Good call — add alert `provenance.attribution.delta > 0.05` to canary dashboard.

sam: LGTM.
